Node built-ins only, no console.log, exact assertions, files under 450 lines, functions under 50 lines. Apply this reviewer fix list (line numbers approximate). Read test/cli-helpers.mjs, test/cli-io.test.mjs, test/cli-errors.test.mjs and .team/near-miss/run-near-miss.mjs fully first.

test/cli-helpers.mjs
1. Add `runAsync(args, { stdinOpen = false, timeoutMs = 10000 } = {})` using child_process.spawn(process.execPath, [CLI, ...args], { stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] }): collect stdout/stderr as utf8 strings; if stdinOpen is false end stdin immediately, otherwise leave the stdin pipe open (never write, never end) until the child exits; resolve { status, stdout, stderr, timedOut } on 'close'; if timeoutMs passes first, kill the child (SIGKILL) and resolve with timedOut: true. Clear the timer on close; reject on 'error'. Keep it under 40 lines.

test/cli-errors.test.mjs
2. (step order, ~line 267) add: "the document is not read before the patch passes": write a bad patch file ('nope'), `const r = await runAsync([p], { stdinOpen: true, timeoutMs: 10000 })`; assert r.timedOut === false, then assertFailure(r, 3, `Error: ${p}: invalid JSON`). Same with args [p, '-'] and with a too-deep patch file (expected 'too deep').
3. (usage/args, ~line 30) add tests that only exactly '-' means stdin: run(['--'], ...) with cwd: dir and doc given -> e.g. run(['--', 'doc.json'], {cwd: dir}) -> exit 1 'Error: --: no such file'; ['./-', doc] -> 'Error: ./-: no such file'; [okPatch, '--'] -> 'Error: --: no such file'; ['', doc] -> 'Error: : no such file'. Also a real file literally named '-x' works: writeFile(dir,'-x','[]') then run(['-x', 'doc.json'],{cwd:dir}) succeeds.
4. (~line 210) drop the shared mutable counter `k`; build file names from the shape label (e.g. label.replace(/\W+/g,'-')) plus the depth.
5. (~line 229-238) delete the duplicate scalar/objNest depth tests already covered by the shape table (keep the 1000/1001 shape table and the 'patch 1001 deep', '[{}]', huge-depth tests). Remove objNest if unused.
6. (~line 66) chmod catch: `catch (err) { t.skip(\`chmod failed: ${err.code}\`); return; }`.
7. (~line 94) the comment above the todo test: drop the line-number reference; describe the behaviour: "Known CLI bug: Node's process.stdin ends without error on a directory fd, so the CLI reports invalid JSON (exit 3) instead of cannot read (exit 1)."

test/cli-io.test.mjs
8. (~line 9) rename `j` (JSON.stringify) to `toJson` everywhere in this file.
9. (~line 177) rename "does not read the document when the patch is fine but applies cleanly" to "an empty patch on a scalar document prints the document".
10. (~line 183-191) delete the two step-order tests duplicated in cli-errors.test.mjs; if the describe becomes a single test, move it into the 'success inputs' describe and delete the empty describe.

.team/near-miss/run-near-miss.mjs
11. (~line 66) report a timed-out run as `TIMEOUT` (status null / error code ETIMEDOUT) — counted as killed for the survivors count but labelled TIMEOUT in the output line; if a run throws (spawn failure), restore originals (already in finally), remove the backup temp dir, write one plain line `error: <message>` to stderr and exit 2 (no stack trace). Keep functions small.

Report the exact changes per item.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

All 11 items are applied. I couldn't run anything here, so none of it has been run, including the new tests. **`/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/test/cli-helpers.mjs`** 1. I added `runAsync(args, { stdinOpen = false, timeoutMs = 10000 })` and imported `spawn`. - It spawns the CLI with `stdio` set to three pipes and collects stdout and stderr as utf8. - With `stdinOpen` false it ends stdin at once. Otherwise stdin stays open and is never written or ended. - It resolves `{ status, stdout, stderr, timedOut }` on `close`. After `timeoutMs` it sends SIGKILL and sets `timedOut: true`. - The timer is cleared on `close` and on `error`, and `error` rejects. - I added one thing you didn't ask for: a no-op `stdin` error listener when stdin is held open. Without it, an EPIPE on the killed child's stdin would crash the test process. If you'd rather not have it, delete the `else child.stdin.on('error', () => {})` line. **`/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/test/cli-errors.test.mjs`** 2. In the `step order` describe I added a nested describe, "the document is not read before the patch passes". - It covers two patches, `'nope'` (invalid JSON) and `nest(1001)` (too deep), each with args `[p]` and `[p, '-']`, so four tests. - Each test calls `runAsync` with `stdinOpen: true`, asserts `timedOut === false`, then asserts `assertFailure(r, 3, 'Error:

: ')`. - File names are built from the label and the arg count. - I added the `assert` and `runAsync` imports. 3. In the `usage` describe I added a nested describe, "only exactly "-" means stdin". Every test runs with `cwd: dir` and a `stdin-doc.json` file written by a `withDoc` helper. - `['--', doc]` gives exit 1 with `Error: --: no such file`. - `['./-', doc]` gives exit 1 with `Error: ./-: no such file`. - `['ok-patch.json', '--']` gives exit 1 with `Error: --: no such file`. - `['', doc]` gives exit 1 with `Error: : no such file`. - A real file named `-x` containing `[]`, run as `['-x', doc]`, succeeds with `{}`. 4. I removed the shared counter `k`. File names are now `deep-ok-${slug}-1000.json` and `deep-bad-${slug}-1001.json`, where `slug = label.replace(/\W+/g, '-')`. 5. I deleted the three duplicate depth tests (scalar 1000, scalar 1001 and the objNest pair), and removed `objNest`. The 1000/1001 shape table, "patch 1001 deep", `[{}]` and the huge-depth tests remain. 6. The chmod catch is now `catch (err) { t.skip(\`chmod failed: ${err.code}\`); return; }`. 7. The todo-test comment now reads: "Known CLI bug: Node's process.stdin ends without error on a directory fd, so the CLI reports invalid JSON (exit 3) instead of cannot read (exit 1)." **`/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/test/cli-io.test.mjs`** 8. I deleted the two duplicated step-order tests and the now-empty `step order on success path` describe. **`/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/.team/near-miss/run-near-miss.mjs`** 11. On a throw (for example a spawn failure) it removes the backup temp dir, writes `error: ` to stderr and exits 2. - Originals are still restored by the existing `finally` in `runOne`. **Size check:** I didn't count lines.
